references.text: Psalm 10:16 declares 'The Lord is king forever' (יְהוָ֣ה מֶ֭לֶךְ עוֹלָ֣ם וָעֶ֑ד), using nearly identical language about God's eternal kingdom.
Psalm 29:10 describes the Lord as enthroned as king forever, affirming God's eternal dominion over creation.
Psalm 146:10 proclaims 'The Lord shall be king forever,' directly reflecting the theme of God's eternal kingdom from Moses' song.
Exodus 3:15 introduces YHWH as Israel's God from everlasting to everlasting, establishing the foundation for His eternal dominion praised in 15:18.
Daniel 4:34 declares that God's kingdom is an eternal kingdom and His dominion endures from generation to generation, confirming the eternal kingship.
Revelation 11:15 proclaims that 'The Lord and His Anointed shall reign forever' (βασιλεύσει εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων), fulfilling the promise of God's eternal kingdom.
Revelation 15:3 contains 'Moses' song,' which praises God as 'King of the nations,' linking directly back to the victory song in Exodus 15.
1 Timothy 1:17 praises 'the King of the ages' (τῷ βασιλεῖ τῶν αἰώνων), reflecting the confession of God's eternal kingdom.
Psalm 9:8 connects God's eternal throne from Exodus to His role as eternal judge.
Daniel shows how God's eternal kingdom (Exodus) will be given to the saints of the Most High.
God's eternal reign in Exodus is linked to the messianic promise of David's eternal throne.
The Samuel covenant specifies God's eternal throne from Exodus for the house of David.
